**Finding: deviation (critical) — LOL-CAP**

**What the document does:** The Agreement has no standalone limitation-of-liability section. The only cap is a single all-caps sentence (p0077) tucked at the end of Section 12 (Indemnity):

> IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY ... (OTHER THAN ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.

**Why it fails the fallback:**
1. **One-sided.** Only TrueLink is capped. Our liability is unlimited, including under the very broad Section 12(a) indemnity (any breach, all Client Content claims, product/service injury claims, and System/Credit Repository Agreement defaults). This is the rule's express walk-away scenario.
2. **Scope uncertainty.** The vendor cap is limited to "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" — Sections 3, 4 and 11 do not appear anywhere in the document outline, so even the vendor-side cap is of indeterminate reach while the indemnity is unqualified.
3. **No damages exclusion.** A document-wide search confirms no exclusion of indirect/consequential damages for either party.
4. **No carve-out architecture.** Confidentiality (Section 10), data security, indemnification, fraud and IP infringement are not addressed; the only carve-out runs against TrueLink.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** Single-sentence edit to p0077 — cap made mutual and Agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' hosting/support compensation and USD 1,000,000; mutual indirect-damages exclusion added; an "Excluded Claims" definition placed outside the cap (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement); and our Section 5 payment obligations expressly preserved outside the limitation. Fallback offered in the comment: a straight mutual 12 months' fees cap with indemnity, confidentiality and gross negligence/wilful misconduct carve-outs.

Note: the breadth of the Section 12(a) indemnity itself is a separate issue for the indemnity rule; I have flagged it here only insofar as it drives the uncapped-customer exposure.
